title: Build a Sentence in English
summary: Build short English sentences with questions and answers.

sources.label: British Council Present simple — verb to be
sources.note: Be forms, negatives, questions and short answers.

sources.label: British Council Question forms
sources.note: Be question order and question words.

sources.label: British Council Capital letters and apostrophes
sources.note: Sentence capitals, capital I and names.

cover.alt: Warm, clear illustration of a bright classroom where a teacher welcomes two learners; schoolbags, chairs and picture-only books create a friendly learning scene; no letters, numbers, signs or text

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Today we learn to build short English sentences. We also learn to ask questions and write them.

blocks.title: Part 1: Am, Is and Are
paragraphs: Be tells us who or where someone is.
It also tells us how someone feels.
Use is with he, she and it.
Use are with you, we and they.
Emma is a teacher. She is a teacher.
Ben is here. He is here.
For questions, put am, is or are first.
Answer with I when someone asks about you.
To say no, add not after be.
Keep am in Yes, I am.
Write Are you ready? Put be first.

images.alt: A teacher greeting a boy and a girl beside a classroom window, with sunshine outside; clear faces and gestures show who is speaking and listening; no speech bubbles, letters, numbers or text

items.explanation: Use are with we.
The person tells us which be word to use.
Use is with she.
Use is for Ben, like he.

items.hint: Look at the person before the space.
items.explanation: Use am with I, then add not.
Put are before they in a question.

items.instruction: Answer no about yourself. Use a short answer.
items.explanation: Answer about yourself with I am not.
Use she with is.

blocks.title: Part 2: English Sentence Order
paragraphs: Add other words if you need them.
Put this question word before is.
Study: Read the statement and its two questions.

images.alt: A child reading an open picture-only book at a desk, shown clearly from left to right as the child, the reading action and the book; uncluttered classroom background; no letters, numbers, arrows or text

items.explanation: Start a statement with who or what.
Start a statement with who, but a be question with be.

items.sourceJa: 彼らはサッカーをします。
items.explanation: Put they first, then play, then football.
Put is after where and before my bag.

items.instruction: Change the question to a statement.
items.explanation: Put they before are in a statement.

items.instruction: Ask where the bag is. Keep the bag.
items.explanation: Put where first, then is, then the bag.

blocks.title: Part 3: Be or an Action Verb
paragraphs: Be tells who, where or how.
An action verb tells what someone does.
Walk, play and read show actions.
Use be or an action verb in these sentences.
Wrong: I am go to school.
Do not add am before go.
Study: Read I am ready and I walk.

images.alt: One illustration divided into two clear scenes: a child sitting ready beside a schoolbag, and another child walking along a path toward a school building; no signs, letters, numbers or text

blocks.title: Practice: Be or an Action Verb

items.explanation: Walk shows the action.

items.instruction: Match each word to its sentence.
items.explanation: Be tells how someone feels, and read shows an action.

items.sourceJa: 私は家で本を読みます。
items.explanation: Read is the action verb, so do not add am.
Use play for the action.

items.prompt: Choose am or walk: I ___ ready.
items.hint: This sentence tells how I feel.
items.explanation: Use am to tell how I feel.
Play is the action verb, so remove are.

items.instruction: Choose are or play. Write the complete sentence.
items.explanation: Play shows what they do.

blocks.title: Part 4: Capital Letters and Sentence Endings
paragraphs: A capital letter is a big letter, like A.
Use a big letter to start each sentence.
Names start with big letters too.
End a statement with a full stop.
End a question with a question mark.
Find each big letter, full stop and question mark.

images.alt: Overhead view of a learner's hand holding a pencil above a clean, unmarked notebook, with an eraser and coloured pencils beside it; no letters, numbers, punctuation or text

blocks.title: Practice: Capital Letters and Sentence Endings

items.explanation: Always write I with a capital.

items.instruction: Match each word to its capital form.
items.explanation: Use capitals for I and names.

items.instruction: Make a sentence with a capital and full stop.
items.explanation: Use capital I and end the statement with a full stop.
Always write I with a capital.

items.prompt: Fix the capitals: i am ben. Write: ___
items.hint: Look at the first word and the name.
items.explanation: Use capitals for I and names.

items.instruction: Put the words in order. Add capitals and a full stop.
items.explanation: Start Ben with a capital and add a full stop.

items.instruction: Make a yes/no question. Add a capital and a question mark.
items.explanation: Put Are first and end with a question mark.

blocks.title: Speaking
paragraphs: Tell a partner who and where you are. Ask a question with be. Give short answers. Then change places.

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: You can build, ask and answer.

items.prompt: Which sentence can you write from memory?
Can you change it into a question?
